source.title: The Impact of the Mini-batch Size on the Variance of Gradients in Stochastic Gradient Descent

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports mini-batch size experiments on training-to-test accuracy gaps, using different models and settings from the claim versions’ original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper’s theory and experiments on gradient variance do not by themselves test the listed versions. The MNIST accuracy-gap result directly bears on V5. Figure-only comparisons without textual descriptions are not separately reconstructed. Cited batch-size results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out classification error across batch sizes at matched epochs on MNIST and Yelp. These results bear directly on V5. The record incorrectly treats V5 as a claim about the training–test gap alone.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the gradient-variance conclusion and the qualified MNIST gap finding, but omits the authors' reported decrease in validation classification error with larger batches on MNIST and in validation loss and error on Yelp. Their generalization-gap conjecture remains an empirical observation rather than an analytical result.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch sizes and reports a training-to-test accuracy gap, but its MNIST experiment uses a distorted validation set as the test set and does not report fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons. Its central theoretical and empirical focus is gradient variance.
record.method_sensitivity: For the MNIST accuracy gap, the reported increasing-with-batch-size pattern starts at epoch 500; multiple distortion hyperparameter choices are said to preserve the pattern. Validation loss does not show a decreasing-with-batch-size property when it is stable or increasing.

fits_no_version.finding: The MNIST training–distorted-test accuracy gap increases with batch size from epoch 500 onward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size can increase the training–distorted-test accuracy gap without establishing the direction of held-out accuracy itself.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient variance decreases with batch size in the analytical settings and empirical experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mini-batch size affects gradient variance under the studied assumptions and training recipes.

record.problems: The reported MNIST accuracy-gap values are available only in a figure; the text gives a qualitative trend without exact values or uncertainty. The test set is created by distorting the validation images, and the generalization finding is reported only from epoch 500 onward. The experiments use different settings from the analytical models.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V5 result rows beyond R1: the paper describes the MNIST gap trend qualitatively and Figure 3(b) is the only reported gap result. Other plotted results on gradient variance, loss, and error are not measurements of the training-to-test error gap specified by V5. Figure 5 reports XLNet training-minus-validation accuracy, but the text does not state a batch-size-dependent gap result; no exact values are reconstructed from the figure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Batch sizes beyond an identified workload-dependent threshold; language modeling; interventions testing longer training, learning-rate scaling, normalization, or regularization. Yelp sentiment classification is not language modeling.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons of generalization measures.

missing.what: Direct MNIST validation classification-error comparison: the authors report decreasing error with increasing batch size. Although rows_left_out declares its exclusion, the stated justification is incorrect: V5 concerns held-out performance, not exclusively a training–test gap.

Direct Yelp validation loss and classification-error comparisons for batches 32 and 64 over 20 epochs. These are relevant V5 results despite the record's blanket exclusion of loss and error plots. The prose reports decreasing error; the figure caption refers to accuracy, so numerical ordering should be checked when reconstructing rows.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text includes figure captions but no readable plotted values. Verdicts therefore rely on explicit prose and the common epoch budgets in Appendix B. The tested batch ranges do not establish behavior beyond a workload-dependent threshold.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label memorization/generalization comparison.
No sweep over network width or interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance under limited tuning.

The reported generalization-gap result is for MNIST, with a distorted validation set as test set, at epochs 500 onward; other workload-dependent batch thresholds, language models, fixed epoch comparisons across batches, and recipe adaptations are not tested.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

rows.subject: three-layer fully connected neural network with 1024, 512 and 10 neurons in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared training-to-test accuracy gap across mini-batch sizes; the text describes the gap as increasing with batch size starting at epoch 500.

conditions.value: gap of accuracy for batch size 128

rows.measure: Gap between training and test accuracies, used as a measure of generalization ability.
rows.baseline: batch size 128; exact gap value not stated
rows.value: batch size 64 had a smaller gap than batch size 128 starting at epoch 500; exact values not stated
rows.note: The paper says the gap is an increasing function of batch size starting at epoch 500, partially aligning with its conjecture. Exact numerical values are not given.
rows.check: A larger training–test accuracy gap does not establish worse held-out accuracy when training accuracy also changes. This row cannot determine V5. Appendix B.3 also establishes a common 1,000-epoch budget, contrary to the record's statement that fixed-epoch comparisons were not reported.

rows.subject: three-layer fully connected neural network with 1024, 512 and 10 neurons in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared expected validation loss across mini-batch sizes; the text reports no decreasing property when validation loss stabilizes or increases.

conditions.value: loss tends to be stable or increasing; model starts to be over-fitting

rows.value: The decreasing property with batch size does not hold when validation loss tends to be stable or increasing.
rows.note: This result concerns validation loss, not the training-to-test error gap named in V5; the authors describe the trend qualitatively.
rows.check: Validation loss is a held-out performance measure relevant to V5. However, the statement that its decreasing trend fails during overfitting does not specify whether larger batches produce equal, higher, or inconsistently ordered validation loss.

relationships.condition: MNIST fully connected classifier, batches 64 and 128, common 1,000-epoch training budget
relationships.reason: Section 4.2 explicitly reports lower validation classification error with larger batches; this qualifies a broad batch-size penalty, although no harmful-size threshold is established. Based on text missing from the rows; R1's gap cannot establish the opposite.
relationships.display_finding: Lower validation classification error with larger batches was reported, but the direct comparison remains unverified. It does not identify a batch size above which error increases.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: MNIST fully connected classifier, batches 64 and 128, common 1,000-epoch training budget
source_check.reason: Lower validation error at batch 128 is explicitly reported, but neither tested size is established as beyond a harmful workload-dependent threshold. This does not qualify the already conditional V5 claim.

relationships.condition: Yelp sentiment classification with XLNet and Adam, batches 32 and 64, common 20-epoch budget
relationships.reason: Section 4.2 reports decreasing validation loss and error as batch size increases, showing a setting without the proposed penalty over the tested range. Based on text missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Decreasing validation loss and error with larger batches were reported, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Yelp sentiment classification with XLNet and Adam, batches 32 and 64, common 20-epoch budget
source_check.reason: The improvement is reported, but no harmful-size threshold is established. Moreover, this experiment measures sentiment classification rather than held-out language-model performance; it does not establish a limitation of V5 as worded.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study reports its own training and validation loss and classification-error comparisons across batch sizes.

tranche.reason: Its empirical batch-size comparisons measure held-out performance at matched epochs, bearing on the same question through a different experimental approach.

source_check.notes: R2's note misdescribes V5 as a training–test gap claim; V5 concerns held-out performance. The direct validation-error comparisons are missing from the listed row; the distorted-test accuracy gap is a separate measure.

statements.correction: MNIST: validation classification error decreases with batch size; batches 64 and 128; 1,000 epochs. Yelp sentiment classification: validation loss and error decrease with batch size; batches 32 and 64; 20 epochs. No harmful-size threshold established; no held-out language-model pretraining loss measured.
statements.problem: The reported comparisons are accurate, but their limits_scope interpretation addresses an unconditional batch-size penalty rather than V5's penalty beyond a workload-dependent size.

reader_labels.condition: MNIST accuracy gap, distorted validation set, epochs 500 onward
reader_labels.reason: The gap increased with batch size in this setting, but the authors describe the result as only partially aligned with the generalization conjecture (R1).
